[Resource from qmd at qmd://t4-qmd/apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/one-to-one-relations.mdx] 1: ---
2: title: One-to-one relations
3: description: How to define and work with one-to-one relations in Prisma.
4: url: /orm/v7/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/one-to-one-relations
5: metaDescription: How to define and work with one-to-one relations in Prisma.
6: metaTitle: One-to-one relations
7: ---
8: 
9: One-to-one (1-1) relations connect at most **one** record on each side. In this example, `User` and `Profile` have a 1-1 relation:
10: 
11: ```prisma
12: model User {
13:   id      Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
14:   profile Profile?
15: }
16: 
17: model Profile {
18:   id     Int  @id @default(autoincrement())
19:   user   User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
20:   userId Int  @unique // Foreign key with unique constraint
21: }
22: ```
23: 
24: This expresses:
25: 
26: - A user can have zero or one profile
27: - A profile must always be connected to exactly one user
28: 
29: You can also reference a non-ID field with `@unique`:
30: 
31: ```prisma
32: model Profile {
33:   id        Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
34:   user      User   @relation(fields: [userEmail], references: [email])
35:   userEmail String @unique
36: }
37: ```
38: 
39: ## Multi-field relations (relational databases only)
40: 
41: ```prisma
42: model User {
43:   firstName String
44:   lastName  String
45:   profile   Profile?
46:   @@id([firstName, lastName])
47: }
48: 
49: model Profile {
50:   id            Int    @id @default(autoincrement())
51:   user          User   @relation(fields: [userFirstName, userLastName], references: [firstName, lastName])
52:   userFirstName String
53:   userLastName  String
54:   @@unique([userFirstName, userLastName])
55: }
56: ```
57: 
58: ## 1-1 in the database
59: 
60: In SQL, a 1-1 relation requires a `UNIQUE` constraint on the foreign key. Without this, it becomes a 1-n relation.
61: 
62: For MongoDB, documents reference each other by ID:
63: 
64: ```json
65: // User
66: { "_id": { "$oid": "60d58e130011041800d209e1" }, "name": "Bob" }
67: // Profile
68: { "_id": "...", "bio": "I like drawing.", "userId": { "$oid": "60d58e130011041800d209e1" } }
69: ```
70: 
71: ## Required and optional 1-1 relation fields
72: 
73: The side _without_ a relation scalar must be optional:
74: 
75: ```prisma
76: model User {
77:   id      Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
78:   profile Profile? // No relation scalar - must be optional
79: }
80: ```
81: 
82: The side _with_ a relation scalar can be required or optional:
83: 
84: **Mandatory 1-1** (cannot create User without Profile):
85: 
86: ```prisma
87: model User {
88:   id        Int     @id @default(autoincrement())
89:   profile   Profile @relation(fields: [profileId], references: [id])
90:   profileId Int     @unique
91: }
92: ```
93: 
94: **Optional 1-1** (can create User without Profile):
95: 
96: ```prisma
97: model User {
98:   id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
99:   profile   Profile? @relation(fields: [profileId], references: [id])
100:   profileId Int?     @unique
101: }
102: ```
103: 
104: ## Choosing which side stores the foreign key
105: 
106: In 1-1 relations, you can choose which side holds the `@relation` attribute and foreign key. Both approaches are valid:
107: 
108: **Option 1:** Foreign key on `Profile`
109: 
110: ```prisma
111: model User {
112:   id      Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
113:   profile Profile?
114: }
115: 
116: model Profile {
117:   id     Int  @id @default(autoincrement())
118:   user   User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id])
119:   userId Int  @unique
120: }
121: ```
122: 
123: **Option 2:** Foreign key on `User`
124: 
125: ```prisma
126: model User {
127:   id        Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
128:   profile   Profile? @relation(fields: [profileId], references: [id])
129:   profileId Int?     @unique
130: }
131: 
132: model Profile {
133:   id   Int   @id @default(autoincrement())
134:   user User?
135: }
136: ```
137:

[Resource from qmd at qmd://t4-qmd/apps/docs/content/docs/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/index.mdx] 100: This data structure represents a one-to-many relation because multiple `Post` documents refer to the same `User` document.
101: 
102: #### `@db.ObjectId` on IDs and relation scalar fields
103: 
104: If your model's ID is an `ObjectId` (represented by a `String` field), you must add `@db.ObjectId` to the model's ID _and_ the relation scalar field on the other side of the relation:
105: 
106: ```prisma highlight=3,9;normal
107: model User {
108:   id    String @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId
109:   posts Post[] // [!code highlight]
110: }
111: 
112: model Post {
113:   id       String @id @default(auto()) @map("_id") @db.ObjectId
114:   author   User   @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id])
115:   authorId String @db.ObjectId // relation scalar field  (used in the `@relation` attribute above) // [!code highlight]
116: 
117:   title String
118: }
119: ```
120: 
121: ## Relations in Prisma Client
122: 
123: Prisma Client is generated from the Prisma schema. The following examples demonstrate how relations manifest when you use Prisma Client to get, create, and update records.
124: 
125: ### Create a record and nested records
126: 
127: The following query creates a `User` record and two connected `Post` records:
128: 
129: ```ts
130: const userAndPosts = await prisma.user.create({
131:   data: {
132:     posts: {
133:       create: [
134:         { title: "Prisma Day 2020" }, // Populates authorId with user's id
135:         { title: "How to write a Prisma schema" }, // Populates authorId with user's id
136:       ],
137:     },
138:   },
139: });
140: ```
141: 
142: In the underlying database, this query:
143: 
144: 1. Creates a `User` with an auto-generated `id` (for example, `20`)
145: 2. Creates two new `Post` records and sets the `authorId` of both records to `20`
146: 
147: ### Retrieve a record and include related records
148: 
149: The following query retrieves a `User` by `id` and includes any related `Post` records:
150: 
151: ```ts
152: const getAuthor = await prisma.user.findUnique({
153:   where: {
154:     id: "20",
155:   },
156:   include: {
157:     posts: true, // All posts where authorId == 20 // [!code highlight]
158:   },
159: });
160: ```
161: 
162: In the underlying database, this query:
163: 
164: 1. Retrieves the `User` record with an `id` of `20`
165: 2. Retrieves all `Post` records with an `authorId` of `20`
166: 
167: ### Associate an existing record to another existing record
168: 
169: The following query associates an existing `Post` record with an existing `User` record:
170: 
171: ```ts
172: const updateAuthor = await prisma.user.update({
173:   where: {
174:     id: 20,
175:   },
176:   data: {
177:     posts: {
178:       connect: {
179:         id: 4,
180:       },
181:     },
182:   },
183: });
184: ```
185: 
186: In the underlying database, this query uses a [nested `connect` query](/orm/v6/reference/prisma-client-reference#connect) to link the post with an `id` of 4 to the user with an `id` of 20. The query does this with the following steps:
187: 
188: - The query first looks for the user with an `id` of `20`.
189: - The query then sets the `authorID` foreign key to `20`. This links the post with an `id` of `4` to the user with an `id` of `20`.
190: 
191: In this query, the current value of `authorID` does not matter. The query changes `authorID` to `20`, no matter its current value.
192: 
193: ## Types of relations
194: 
195: There are three different types (or [cardinalities](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardinality_(data_modeling)>)) of relations in Prisma ORM:
196: 
197: - [One-to-one](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/one-to-one-relations) (also called 1-1 relations)
198: - [One-to-many](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/one-to-many-relations) (also called 1-n relations)
199: - [Many-to-many](/orm/v6/prisma-schema/data-model/relations/many-to-many-relations) (also called m-n relations)
